svg.title: Web application with two IdP authorities
svg.desc: Two independent ASP.NET Framework 4.8 applications on Windows Azure App Service use OWIN and direct MSAL authorization code with PKCE. Each application has a separate web registration in Workforce tenant and External ID tenant. Employees use workforce identities, partners use workforce B2B only in Sample application 2, and approved retirees and dependents use External ID. Server-side entitlements control business access. Managed identities call workforce Microsoft Graph and Azure Communication Services Email. A separate provisioner and native password setup client support sponsored registration. A third, separately protected App Service hosts the operator driver. Documentation snapshot dated 9 October 2026; recipient redemption and real partner admission remain pending.
svg.text: CUSTOMER ARCHITECTURE · IMPLEMENTED POC
Web application with two IdP authorities
ASP.NET Framework 4.8 / IIS · shared authentication code, separate identities and sessions
Employees
Workforce tenant · Sample applications 1 and 2
Signed Employee role + current approval in each app
Organizational partners
Workforce B2B · Sample application 2 only
Signed home-organization proof + Partner role + approval
Retirees, dependents and approved externals
External ID tenant · approval is specific to each app
Sponsor required; dependents also need benefit eligibility
Azure application hosting
Two Windows App Services · shared B1 plan · HTTPS · IIS integrated pipeline
Sample application 1
System.Web MVC · independent app cookie and configuration
Exact sign-in UPN → workforce Graph lookup
Found → workforce; confirmed absent → External ID
Lookup failure stops routing; aliases are not resolved.
Employees + approved external personas; partners denied
Sample application 2
System.Web MVC · independent app cookie and configuration
Exact employee / approved partner domain routes
Workforce for those routes; others → External ID
Dynamic partner route requires redeemed current approval.
Adds approved organizational B2B partners
Shared OWIN / Katana + direct MSAL.NET implementation
Authorization code + PKCE; OWIN protects state and nonce
MSAL redeems code using the selected web-client credential
Separate /signin-workforce and /signin-external callbacks
JWT signature, issuer, audience, lifetime + tenant/object ID
Signed persona role + app-specific server-side entitlement
Secure / HttpOnly cookie; source fix caps it at 20 minutes
Routing never grants access. A failed workforce sign-in never switches to External ID.
Server-only configuration and approval state
IIS-protected App_Data
Identity settings, baseline entitlements, registration settings
Credentials supplied through server App Service settings
Persistent data outside wwwroot
Per-app invitations, approvals, token hashes, delivery audit
D:\home\data\… · atomic writes · excluded from deploy ZIP
Workforce OIDC
External ID OIDC
Workforce tenant
Employees, workforce B2B guests and directory assignments
App 1 web registration
Employee role
App 2 web registration
Employee / Partner + capabilities
Each: own client, credential and registered callback
Assignment-required enterprise applications; signed app roles
Partner token identifies the guest in this tenant.
Signed idp must match the approved external home organization.
Email domain or an organizational account alone is insufficient.
External ID tenant
Pre-provisioned customer accounts · email/password user flow
App 1 web registration
Retiree / Dependent / External
App 2 web registration
Retiree / Dependent / External
Each: own client, credential and registered callback
Both web clients are associated with the controlled user flow.
Public sign-up disabled; role assignment + approval still required.
Separate provisioner and public/native setup client, shown below.
Customer identities are distinct from workforce guest identities.
Server-side integration and operator access
Separate from the four interactive web clients
Per-site managed identity
Workforce Microsoft Graph + ACS Email
App 1: exact UPN lookup; current sponsor / role checks
App 2: sponsor checks; B2B invite and Partner assignment
Both: managed email sender sends invitation links
Delivery operation tracked before network submission
Workforce Graph uses app-only tokens; ACS uses Azure RBAC.
External provisioning and account setup
App-only provisioner + separate public/native client
Provisioner: create / locate customer and assign app role
Native SSPR: verify email and set recipient-chosen password
No API permissions on setup client; sign-up stays disabled
Then normal web sign-in + one-use invitation confirmation
Setup does not issue the application's authenticated session.
Separate operator driver App Service
Runbook, architecture and downloadable source
Dedicated Workforce tenant registration and credential
App Service EasyAuth; approved operator object-ID allowlist
All paths protected: pages, assets, catalog, manifest, ZIP
Same hosting plan; independent of the two app sessions
The driver is documentation; it does not grant business access.
Verification boundary
Source snapshot: web-client credentials require renewal; the cookie-cap fix still needs deployment and verification.
Real partner admission and personal recipient account setup / invitation redemption remain pending. Detailed flow and source evidence: CUSTOMER-ARCHITECTURE.md
